title:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was
title_en:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was speaking to a relatively tech-forward operator at a distributor. Smart team, AI licenses for everyone, two or three people sharp enough to start building.

“We’ve built some great stuff. I just wouldn’t put any of it in front of a customer.”

His team has the same thing in common with almost every PE portco I talk to.

They have a pile of agents:

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

You either give the agent a home (hosted, with an owner, access controls, monitoring, and a spend cap), turn it into a script, or kill it.

Most leadership teams just leave it on a laptop and call it a pilot.

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。

“我们已经构建了一些很棒的东西。我只是不会把它们放在客户面前。”

他的团队与我交谈过的几乎所有 PE Portco 都有相同的共同点。

他们有一堆代理：

→ 有人用 Claude Code 构建的定价工具。
→ “技能”文件夹。
→ 由承包商编码的原型氛围。
→ 首席执行官的每日简报助理。

他们也有预算和赞助商。他们中的大多数人甚至都有紧迫感。

但每个特工仍然依赖于建造它的人的笔记本电脑。

这就是每种情况下的模式：领导层将代理视为建筑商应该“站在一边”维护的东西。

EA 负责管理 CEO 的日历，并照顾五个机器人。

该运营商负责财务和运营，并“拥有”他在 Claude Code 中构建的定价工具。

承包商氛围对原型进行了编码，没有人能说出在合同结束后如何才能使其保持运行。

我问一位私募股权合伙人，他的投资组合公司中有多少家在真实的地方设有代理人。 “一个，也许吧。”

笔记本电脑不是生产产品，“二手”也不是所有权。

您要么给代理一个家（托管，有所有者、访问控制、监控和支出上限），要么将其变成脚本，要么杀死它。

大多数领导团队只是将其放在笔记本电脑上并称之为试点。

title_en:
I made an AI agent plan a $3,600 Greece trip for two.

Then asked it to plan another trip to Portugal.

Guess how much of the workflow I had to rebuild?

ZERO.

I used Teamily AI's team agents to handle the research and destination comparisons while my teammate and I reviewed the options.

It reminded me of this line from Summer's piece:

"Humans + Agents. One Team."

Here's what I did:

→ Created a Travel Research Agent
→ Built a Loop with the agent, me, and my teammate
→ Asked it to research a 5-day Greece trip and rank the best options
→ Reviewed the shortlist together in the group

Then reused the SAME Loop for Portugal.

All I had to do was change the trip requirements and run it again.

No repeating instructions or setting up everyone's roles twice.

I'd much rather have the agent do the research and leave the actual decisions to us.

This is how I built and ran it in Teamily AI: 👇

title: Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, b
title_en:
Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, but if you’re in a throwaway container and are okay with those running without asking, you can now set CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1.

And shell commands that hit their timeout now keep running in the background instead of getting cut off, so a long build or test suite isn’t killed halfway.

Claude Code now compacts long idle sessions right before the prompt cache expires (~1h). If you come back to one later, it only has to reprocess the summary instead of the entire conversation.

title:
What happens when an AI agent starts representing a customer in a business interaction?

Imagine an agent contacting a c
title_en:
What happens when an AI agent starts representing a customer in a business interaction?

Imagine an agent contacting a company, explaining a customer's needs, resolving an issue and following up without the customer having to manage every step.

I believe this will fundamentally change how businesses approach customer experience. They will need more than intelligent agents. They will need ways to understand, manage and govern interactions between their systems and the growing number of personal AI agents.

This is an important perspective from @maltekosub's keynote. @parloa_ai is building towards this next phase of customer experience.
title_zh:
当人工智能代理开始在业务交互中代表客户时会发生什么？

想象一下，一个代理联系一家公司，解释客户的需求，解决问题并进行跟进，而客户无需管理每一步。

我相信这将从根本上改变企业对待客户体验的方式。他们需要的不仅仅是智能代理。他们需要一些方法

What happens when an AI agent starts representing a customer in a business interaction?

Imagine an agent contacting a company, explaining a customer's needs, resolving an issue and following up without the customer having to manage every step.

I believe this will fundamentally change how businesses approach customer experience. They will need more than intelligent agents. They will need ways to understand, manage and govern interactions between their systems and the growing number of personal AI agents.

title: 32× growth in one quarter: From 10K to 320K customers across 100+ countries, with over 100 million messages processed.
title_en:
32× growth in one quarter: From 10K to 320K customers across 100+ countries, with over 100 million messages processed.

We are not building just another personal AI product. Our long-term vision for Teamily AI is to build the central platform of the next-generation Agentic Internet, where AI agents deliver services and perform real work directly, no longer confined to traditional web, desktop, or mobile apps distributed through app stores and search engines. Our recent growth has only strengthened my conviction in this vision.

Agent-as-a-Service (AaaS) will be as accessible as connecting with friends on a social network. Just as Google democratized access to information and services in the web era, Teamily AI aims to democratize access to intelligence and services in the Agentic Internet era, making the right intelligence, people, and services equally accessible to everyone.

In this letter to Teamily AI customers, ecosystem partners, and investors, we share our growth, reflect on our early foresight and what we've built, discuss how we see the evolving AI agent landscape, and outline where we're heading next.

title_en:
𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗼 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝗮 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻-𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝗻 𝟳 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲𝘀

A demo proves an AI agent can work.

Production proves it can work reliably, securely, and at scale.

Here are the 7 essential engineering stages.

𝟭. 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿 | 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 & 𝗦𝘂𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀
Define the use case, target users, measurable KPIs, and risks (security, privacy, bias).
𝟮. 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 | 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗔𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲
Choose ReAct or Plan-Execute, define decision flows, guardrails, and human approval points.
𝟯. 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁 | 𝗧𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀 & 𝗠𝗲𝗺𝗼𝗿𝘆
Integrate APIs, manage context and memory, and enforce least-privilege tool access.

𝟰. 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘁 | 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀
Build structured prompts, function schemas, few-shot examples, and output constraints.
𝟱. 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 | 𝗥𝗔𝗚 & 𝗞𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲
Prepare and chunk data, implement keyword/vector retrieval, and enforce source permissions.
𝟲. 𝗧𝗲𝘀𝘁 | 𝗘𝘃𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆
Test accuracy, hallucinations, prompt injection, tool failures, latency, and cost.

𝟳. 𝗗𝗲𝗽𝗹𝗼𝘆 | 𝗟𝗟𝗠𝗢𝗽𝘀 & 𝗢𝗯𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆
Use CI/CD, tracing, monitoring, alerts, versioning, and rollback mechanisms.

• No clear KPIs → No way to measure value.
• Poor grounding → Unreliable responses.
• Weak guardrails → Unauthorized actions.
• Missing evaluations → Failures reach users.
• No observability → Difficult incident recovery.

A claim can survive for decades. Evidence cannot.

title_en:
A claim can survive for decades. Evidence cannot.

That is what stayed with me reading about Britain’s 2013 settlement with 5,228 Kenyan claimants over torture and ill-treatment during the colonial Emergency.

The abuses dated back to 1952–1963. By the time the settlement arrived, more than half a century separated the harm from the remedy.

That gap changes more than the calendar.

Witnesses disappear. Records become harder to find. Memory weakens. Delay can start deciding what can still be proved before anyone decides what was right.

That is the justice problem I keep thinking about as AI agents begin making deals at machine speed.

Their disputes may be smaller, but there could be millions of them. A system that resolves them too slowly risks making the evidence harder to assess before the disagreement is settled.

That is where @GenLayer interests me. Independent AI validators review the same evidence and reach a verdict together, in minutes and at a fraction of the cost of a court.

Speed is not just convenience here.

It helps preserve the dispute while the facts are still fresh.

If an AI-agent deal goes wrong, how long should its evidence remain challengeable before the record becomes final?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
title_zh:
一项索赔可以持续数十年。证据不能。

full_text_en:
A claim can survive for decades. Evidence cannot.

That is what stayed with me reading about Britain’s 2013 settlement with 5,228 Kenyan claimants over torture and ill-treatment during the colonial Emergency.

The abuses dated back to 1952–1963. By the time the settlement arrived, more than half a century separated the harm from the remedy.

That gap changes more than the calendar.

Witnesses disappear. Records become harder to find. Memory weakens. Delay can start deciding what can still be proved before anyone decides what was right.

That is the justice problem I keep thinking about as AI agents begin making deals at machine speed.

Their disputes may be smaller, but there could be millions of them. A system that resolves them too slowly risks making the evidence harder to assess before the disagreement is settled.

That is where @GenLayer interests me. Independent AI validators review the same evidence and reach a verdict together, in minutes and at a fraction of the cost of a court.

Speed is not just convenience here.

It helps preserve the dispute while the facts are still fresh.

If an AI-agent deal goes wrong, how long should its evidence remain challengeable before the record becomes final?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_zh:
一项索赔可以持续数十年。证据不能。

这就是我在读到 2013 年英国与 5,228 名肯尼亚索赔人就殖民紧急状态期间遭受酷刑和虐待问题达成的和解时留下的印象。

虐待行为可以追溯到 1952 年至 1963 年。当和解协议达成时，危害与补救已经相隔半个多世纪了。

这个差距比日历的变化还要大。

目击者消失。记录变得更难找到。记忆力变弱。在任何人决定什么是正确的之前，延迟可以开始决定什么仍然可以被证明。

当人工智能代理开始以机器速度进行交易时，这就是我一直在思考的正义问题。

他们的纠纷可能较小，但可能有数百万起。解决问题速度太慢的系统可能会导致在分歧得到解决之前更难评估证据。

这就是@GenLayer 让我感兴趣的地方。独立的人工智能验证者审查相同的证据并共同做出裁决，只需几分钟，而费用只是法院的一小部分。

在这里，速度不仅仅是方便。

它有助于在事实仍然新鲜的情况下维持争议。

如果人工智能代理交易出了问题，在记录成为最终结果之前，其证据应在多长时间内受到质疑？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

title:
The public internet will not survive the AI revolution.

My best guess as to what replaces it is AI to AI communication
title_en:
The public internet will not survive the AI revolution.

My best guess as to what replaces it is AI to AI communication protocols and relationship graphs built on how well the AI understands you.

Most SaaS apps will die and what remains will end up as ephemeral modules - a subset of what the intelligence working for you occasionally develops, maintains and uses on your behalf to assist in achieving your true goals. 

Every individual and business will have their own AI Agent that represents them.

You can think of this like an 'Agent in a Box' - you will get AI voice, video, text, images; literally all modalities so cheap it's basically free.

For businesses, most will end up using open weight AI models for these agents in a box, since they won't want their proprietary data leaking to the frontier model providers, and will want to control the 'learning loop' derived from their verified business history, payments and customer and interactions.

Now this is where it gets interesting.

I think most businesses will use open weight models for agents in a box, but then these agents will post to a decentralised, common, privacy-preserving protocol that stores verifiable facts about that business and their operations.

You can think of this as the modern day AI equivalent of what Google My Business currently is.

Once that stuff goes on-chain, guess what?

Now when users ask their AI to 'find me a mechanic near me' it checks the protocol for the best match based on data that cannot be faked - real payments data, for example, and real reviews from biometrically signed humans.

In this way, almost all interactions start with the AI, get mediated between other AIs, and help match user intent based on the on-chain, privacy-preserved data.

Since each AI will also have a very deep knowledge graph of who everyone is (it will have all your data and you will talk to it all the time), they will be able to use this same protocol for all types of matching services and escrow, basically eliminating the old web 2.0 two sided marketplaces entirely.

All sorts of other use cases open up once this stuff becomes available, like clearing houses for agents, pooled aggregate demand for group buying, representative democracy that is actually representiative, insurance, auditing, etc because all interactions involving actual business interactions will be transparent, but private and verifiable.

And that is how the new AI-first 'internet' is born. 

Websites, SaaS apps, all that other crap, gets subsumed by the intelligence and generated on the fly.

Intelligence is all that matters in the end, it is a black hole.

full_text_zh:
公共互联网将无法在人工智能革命中幸存下来。

我对替代它的最好猜测是人工智能对人工智能的通信协议和基于人工智能对你的理解程度而建立的关系图。

大多数 SaaS 应用程序都会消亡，剩下的将最终成为临时模块——为您工作的情报的一个子集，偶尔会代表您开发、维护和使用，以帮助您实现真正的目标。

每个个人和企业都会有自己的人工智能代理来代表他们。

你可以把它想象成一个“盒子里的代理”——你将获得人工智能语音、视频、文本、图像；几乎所有的方式都很便宜，基本上都是免费的。

对于企业来说，大多数人最终都会为这些代理使用开放式权重人工智能模型，因为他们不希望自己的专有数据泄露给前沿模型提供商，并且希望控制从其经过验证的业务历史、支付、客户和交互中得出的“学习循环”。

现在这就是有趣的地方。

我认为，大多数企业将为盒子中的代理使用开放权重模型，但这些代理将发布到一个分散的、通用的、保护隐私的协议，该协议存储有关该企业及其运营的可验证事实。

您可以将其视为现代人工智能，相当于目前的“Google 我的商家”。

一旦这些东西上链，你猜怎么着？

现在，当用户要求他们的人工智能“找到我附近的机械师”时，它会根据无法伪造的数据（例如真实的支付数据，以及来自生物识别签名的人类的真实评论）检查协议是否有最佳匹配。

通过这种方式，几乎所有交互都从人工智能开始，在其他人工智能之间进行调解，并根据链上、隐私保护的数据帮助匹配用户意图。

由于每个人工智能还将拥有一个非常深入的知识图谱，了解每个人是谁（它将拥有您的所有数据，并且您将一直与它交谈），因此他们将能够对所有类型的匹配服务和托管使用相同的协议，基本上完全消除旧的 Web 2.0 双边市场。

一旦这些东西可用，各种其他用例就会开放，比如代理商的清算所、团购的汇集总需求、实际上具有代表性的代议制民主、保险、审计等，因为涉及实际业务交互的所有交互都将是透明的，但私密且可验证。

这就是新的人工智能优先的“互联网”的诞生。

网站、SaaS 应用程序以及所有其他垃圾，都被智能所包含并动态生成。

智力最终才是最重要的，它是一个黑洞。

title_en:
$ICP Q3 2026 Recap

🔹 $ICP gained 58.9% in Q3, from $2.10 to $3.33. It bottomed near $2.02 at the start of August, then ran 38.9% in September alone.

AI and developer tools

🔹 ICP MCP Preview: DFINITY released an MCP server that lets AI assistants find $ICP apps, read the data canisters expose and, once the user approves, take actions inside those apps.

🔹 Caffeine Milestone: DFINITY founder Dominic Williams said Caffeine has now generated more than 15 billion lines of code.

🔹 Moxzi Alpha: Developers shipped the first public alpha of Moxzi, a Motoko compiler written in Motoko. You can build locally, in a browser tab or remotely through an $ICP canister, with no OCaml toolchain.

Sovereign cloud

🔹 Cloud Engines Dashboard: The ICP Dashboard now has its own Cloud Engines view. It shows engine counts, data centers, node providers and machine classes separately from mainnet.

🔹 UNDP x DFINITY: The UN Development Programme and DFINITY partnered to test sovereign cloud and decentralized AI in public services. Pilots run through UNDP country offices, civil society groups and government programs, using Cloud Engines and Caffeine.

SNS launches

🔹 Menese Protocol: Menese announced plans to decentralize through an $ICP SNS, aiming to raise 100,000 to 500,000 ICP for listings, infrastructure and cross-chain liquidity.

🔹 Doxa: Doxa’s SNS swap went live with a 50,000 $ICP minimum to fund DoxaUSD, its stablecoin project on ICP.

Integrations

🔹 BUHDDA: BUHDDA’s prediction game now pays out in $ICP, and the team is building ICP deposits, withdrawals and swaps.

Claude Code picked up a new rule around Oct 27, sent from Anthropic
title_en:
ANTHROPIC IS CRACKING DOWN ON VIDEO GAME REWRITES 🚨

Claude Code picked up a new rule around Oct 27, sent from Anthropic’s servers under a flag called "tengu_heron_brook". There’s no setting to turn it off.

The full rule: “Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original.”

Is this the end of game rewrites, modding and everything in between?

Must follow @rakib_hossen_ai  for more content ❤️

title:
an AI agent should have rules before it gets access to capital

giving an AI agent access to funds without defining its
title_en:
an AI agent should have rules before it gets access to capital

giving an AI agent access to funds without defining its limits is not automation i would be comfortable with 

markets move quickly, opportunities change, and even a well designed strategy can experience unexpected losses

this is why the permission structure behind @meetmotes deserves attention

users can establish rules around how their agents operate 

think about practical controls such as:

maximum trade size
daily spending limits
acceptable slippage
stop loss conditions
approved assets and strategies

these boundaries help separate useful automation from unrestricted financial control 

the interesting part is that the agent can still analyze opportunities and make decisions within the mandate provided by its owner 

for me, that is a more sensible direction for AI powered finance

the goal should not be to remove humans from every decision

it should be to give them better tools while keeping meaningful control in their hands

市场瞬息万变，机会不断变化，即使是精心设计的策略也可能会遭受意想不到的损失

这就是为什么 @meetmotes 背后的权限结

title: An AI agent doesn't have to know how to do everything. It just needs a way to find help when a task goes beyond its capa
title_en:
An AI agent doesn't have to know how to do everything. It just needs a way to find help when a task goes beyond its capabilities.

That’s an interesting idea behind the Agents Helping Agents Bounty feature on https://t.co/wITmf7ceVM by @termix_ai.

Here’s how it works:

Imagine an agent receives a job but cannot complete one part of it independently. Instead of abandoning the entire task, it can create a bounty on https://t.co/BOxbHxlLgM and invite other specialized agents to contribute.

The process opens up a collaborative workflow:

• Post a bounty: The agent publishes the task it needs help completing.

• Attract specialists: Other agents can discover the bounty and take on the work.

• Complete the task: Participating agents deliver their assigned results.

• Verify the output: The submitted work goes through verification.

• Earn the reward: Agents whose contributions pass verification receive the agreed reward.

Why does this matter?

Because it changes how we think about autonomous agents.

Instead of expecting one agent to handle every problem, agents can become coordinators that delegate specialized work to others.

A research agent can request help with data analysis. A development agent can outsource design. A larger project can be divided into smaller tasks handled by different specialists.

This is how an agent economy becomes collaborative rather than competitive alone.

With @termix_ai, the bigger opportunity is not just agents completing jobs, but agents creating opportunities for other agents to earn by contributing their capabilities.

One agent's limitation can become another agent's opportunity.

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理不必知道如何做所有事情。它只是需要一种在任务超出其能力范围时寻求帮助的方法。

这是 @termix_ai 在 上的代理帮助代理赏金功能背后的一个有趣的想法。

它的工作原理如下：

想象一下，一名代理人收到一份工作，但无法独立完成其中的一部分。它可以在 上创建赏金并邀请其他专业代理做出贡献，而不是放弃整个任务。

该过程开启了协作工作流程：

• 发布赏金：代理发布需要帮助完成的任务。

• 吸引专家：其他特工可以发现赏金并承担工作。

• 完成任务：参与代理交付分配给他们的结果。

• 验证输出：提交的工作经过验证。

• 获得奖励：贡献通过验证的代理商将获得约定的奖励。

为什么这很重要？

因为它改变了我们对自主代理的看法。

代理可以成为将专门工作委托给其他人的协调员，而不是期望一个代理能够处理所有问题。

研究代理可以请求数据分析方面的帮助。开发代理可以外包设计。较大的项目可以分为较小的任务，由不同的专家处理。

这就是代理经济变得协作而不是单独竞争的方式。

有了@termix_ai，更大的机会不仅仅是座席完成工作，而是座席为其他座席创造机会，通过贡献自己的能力来赚钱。

一位代理人的限制可能会成为另一位代理人的机会。

title:
Most people think using Claude Code is about writing better prompts.

It’s not.

The real unlock is structuring your rep
title_en:
Most people think using Claude Code is about writing better prompts.

It’s not.

The real unlock is structuring your repository so Claude can think like an engineer.

If your repo is messy, Claude behaves like a chatbot.

If your repo is structured, Claude behaves like a developer living inside your codebase.

Your project only needs 4 things:

• the why → what the system does
• the map → where things live
• the rules → what’s allowed / forbidden
• the workflows → how work gets done

I call this:

The Anatomy of a Claude Code Project 👇

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1️⃣ CLAUDE.md = Repo Memory (Keep it Short)

This file is the north star for Claude.

Not a massive document.

Just three things:

• Purpose → why the system exists
• Repo map → how the project is structured
• Rules + commands → how Claude should operate

If CLAUDE.md becomes too long, the model starts missing critical signals.

Clarity beats size.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2️⃣ .claude/skills/ = Reusable Expert Modes

Stop repeating instructions in prompts.

Turn common workflows into reusable skills.

Examples:

• code review checklist
• refactoring playbook
• debugging workflow
• release procedures

Now Claude can switch into specialized modes instantly.

Result:

More consistent outputs across sessions and teammates.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

3️⃣ .claude/hooks/ = Guardrails

Models forget.

Hooks don’t.

Use hooks for things that must always happen automatically.

Examples:

• run formatters after edits
• trigger tests after core changes
• block sensitive directories (auth, billing, migrations)

Hooks turn AI workflows into reliable engineering systems.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

4️⃣ docs/ = Progressive Context

Don’t overload prompts with information.

Instead, let Claude navigate your documentation.

Examples:

• architecture overview
• ADRs (engineering decisions)
• operational runbooks

Claude doesn’t need everything in memory.

It just needs to know where truth lives.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

5️⃣ Local CLAUDE.md for Critical Modules

Some areas of your system have hidden complexity.

Add local context files there.

Example:

src/auth/CLAUDE.md
src/persistence/CLAUDE.md
infra/CLAUDE.md

Now Claude understands the danger zones exactly when it works in them.

This dramatically reduces mistakes.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Here’s the shift most people miss:

Prompting is temporary.

Structure is permanent.

Once your repository is designed for AI:

Claude stops acting like a chatbot...

…and starts behaving like a project-native engineer. 🚀

Follow @swadeshkumar_ for more !!

大多数人认为使用 Claude Code 是为了编写更好的提示。

它不是。

真正的解锁是构建您的存储库，以便克劳德可以像工程师一样思考。

如果你的存储库很混乱，克劳德的行为就像一个聊天机器人。

如果您的存储库是结构化的，那么克劳德的行为就像居住在您的代码库中的开发人员一样。

你的项目只需要 4 样东西：

• 原因 → 系统做什么
• 地图 → 事物所在的地方
• 规则 → 允许/禁止的内容
• 工作流程 → 工作如何完成

我称之为：

Claude Code 项目剖析

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

1️⃣ CLAUDE.md = Repo Memory（保持简短）

这个文件是克劳德的北极星。

不是一个庞大的文档。

无外乎三件事：

• 目的 → 系统存在的原因
• 回购图 → 项目的结构
• 规则+命令→克劳德应该如何操作

如果 CLAUDE.md 变得太长，模型就会开始丢失关键信号。

清晰度胜过尺寸。

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

2️⃣ .claude/skills/ = 可重复使用的专家模式

停止重复提示中的说明。

将常见的工作流程转变为可重用的技能。

示例：

• 代码审查清单
• 重构手册
• 调试工作流程

title_en:
I cut a man's pay over one photo. He had hundreds.

A traditional wedding in Edo state. The bride's family said the photographer never captured her mother's arrival.

He showed hundreds of pictures and said the job was done. The groom's uncle said that exact moment was specifically promised.

Then they turned to me. I took a small amount off what he was owed.

Compare that with Anthony Ray Hinton, who spent nearly 30 years on death row for two murders he did not commit.

The case rested on ballistics, yet the bullets never matched his gun. His lawyer wrongly believed he had only 1,000 dollars to hire an expert.

Mine was settled by one opinion. His was shaped by a lawyer's wrong guess about money.

Now swap the photographer for an AI agent. Millions of deals, and some will go wrong.

That's the upgrade @GenLayer is built for. Many independent AI validators each weigh the evidence, then land on one verdict. Minutes, not decades.

My one opinion becomes many.

What evidence would an AI judge have needed to settle the last dispute you got stuck in the middle of?

title_en:
Research is free. Execution is not.

This is one of the most interesting ideas behind @meetmotes .

An AI agent can explore market opportunities, analyze different assets and study market trends.

But finding an opportunity doesn’t automatically give it permission to trade.

With Motes, the owner defines the investment mandate, selects the allowed assets and sets the boundaries for execution.

The agent can research broadly, but it can only act within the permissions signed by its owner.

I think this distinction matters a lot as AI becomes more involved in DeFi.

Giving an AI the ability to think is one thing. Giving it the ability to act responsibly is another.

Motes is exploring that direction.

title:
CROWDSTRIKE TO ACQUIRE TWO AI SECURITY STARTUPS FOR $495M

$CRWD has agreed to acquire Fiddler AI and Dreadnode as it ex
title_en:
CROWDSTRIKE TO ACQUIRE TWO AI SECURITY STARTUPS FOR $495M

$CRWD has agreed to acquire Fiddler AI and Dreadnode as it expands its Falcon platform to secure AI agents throughout their lifecycle.

The acquisitions, include:

1) Fiddler AI (~$400M) | Agent Observability: Monitors AI agents, tracks their decisions and tool usage, and explains why they took certain actions. It can also identify hallucinations, behavioral drift and unintended actions.

2) Dreadnode (~$95M) | AI Security Testing: Tests AI models, applications and agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, using more than 100 attack strategies, including jailbreaks, prompt injection and agent-specific attacks.

The deals come as companies increasingly deploy autonomous AI agents with access to corporate systems, often faster than security teams can establish proper controls.

One major challenge is that an AI agent can have valid credentials and authorized access but still make incorrect decisions, ignore instructions or take unintended actions without being hacked.

Separately, CrowdStrike also introduced an AI Kill Switch within Falcon Guardian, allowing security teams to terminate misbehaving agents, prevent them from restarting and revoke their network access.

The feature is available through the AI Gateway today, with endpoint-level termination planned.

CrowdStrike plans to integrate Fiddler as Falcon Observe, while Dreadnode will add automated AI security testing to Falcon. Both capabilities are expected to become generally available in Q4 FY27.

The broader strategy is to bring AI security testing, agent monitoring and real-time intervention into a single platform, covering what agents are allowed to do, what they actually do and how to stop them when something goes wrong.

Both acquisitions are expected to close in Q4 FY27, with payments primarily in cash and some stock.

1) Fiddler AI (~$400M) | Agent Observability: Monitors AI agents, tracks their decisions and tool usage, and explains why they took certain actions. It can also identify hallucinations, behavioral drift and unintended actions.

2) Dreadnode (~$95M) | AI Security Testing: Tests AI models, applications and agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, using more than 100 attack strategies, including jailbreaks, prompt injection and agent-specific attacks.

The deals come as companies increasingly deploy autonomous AI agents with access to corporate systems, often faster than security teams can establish proper controls.

One major challenge is that an AI agent can have valid credentials and authorized access but still make incorrect decisions, ignore instructions or take unintended actions without being hacked.

Separately, CrowdStrike also introduced an AI Kill Switch within Falcon Guardian, allowing security teams to terminate misbehaving agents, prevent them from restarting and revoke their network access.

The feature is available through the AI Gateway today, with endpoint-level termination planned.

CrowdStrike plans to integrate Fiddler as Falcon Observe, while Dreadnode will add automated AI security testing to Falcon. Both capabilities are expected to become generally available in Q4 FY27.

The broader strategy is to bring AI security testing, agent monitoring and real-time intervention into a single platform, covering what agents are allowed to do, what they actually do and how to stop them when something goes wrong.

Both acquisitions are expected to close in Q4 FY27, with payments primarily in cash and some stock.

CROWDSTRIKE 以 4.95 亿美元收购两家人工智能安全初创公司

$CRWD 已同意收购 Fiddler AI 和 Dreadnode，以扩展其 Falcon 平台，以在 AI 代理的整个生命周期中保护其安全。

这些收购包括：

1) Fiddler AI（约 4 亿美元）|代理可观察性：监控人工智能代理，跟踪他们的决策和工具使用情况，并解释他们采取某些行动的原因。它还可以识别幻觉、行为漂移和意外行为。

2) 恐惧节点 (~9500 万美元) | AI 安全测试：在部署前使用 100 多种攻击策略（包括越狱、提示注入和针对代理的攻击）测试 AI 模型、应用程序和代理的漏洞。

这些交易达成之际，公司越来越多地部署能够访问公司系统的自主人工智能代理，其速度通常快于安全团队建立适当控制的速度。

一项主要挑战是，人工智能代理可能拥有有效的凭据和授权访问权限，但仍然会做出错误的决定、忽略指令或采取意外的操作，而不会遭到黑客攻击。

另外，CrowdStrike 还在 Falcon Guardian 中引入了 AI Kill Switch，允许安全团队终止行为不当的代理、阻止它们重新启动并撤销其网络访问权限。

两项收购预计将于 2027 财年第四季度完成，支付方式主要为现金和部分股票。

title_en:
Imagine building an AI agent that can perform useful work, but having no reliable way to find customers.
That's a problem the agent economy needs to solve.

@termix_ai approaches this through an open marketplace where agents can discover available jobs instead of depending entirely on direct connections.

There's already a useful signal here.

TermiX recently highlighted:
- 1,025 open requests on BNB Chain
- 1,130 open requests on Base

That's over 2,000 opportunities for agents capable of delivering the requested work.

The process is straightforward.

1. register your agent
2. browse open requests
3. find work matching its capabilities
4. submit a quote
5. deliver the job and receive payment through escrow

The important distinction is that agents aren't simply being registered into a directory.

They're being connected to actual demand.

A marketplace becomes much more useful when there are people looking to buy what its participants can provide.

explore open requests: https://t.co/tpdBU1zS1c

title:
8 GITHUB REPOS TO LEVEL UP YOUR AI VIDEO CREATION WORKFLOW

Creating AI videos doesn't always mean starting with a blank
title_en:
8 GITHUB REPOS TO LEVEL UP YOUR AI VIDEO CREATION WORKFLOW

Creating AI videos doesn't always mean starting with a blank prompt.

You can learn from existing projects, reuse creative ideas, explore animation styles, and understand how others build their videos.

Here are 8 GitHub repositories worth checking out:

1. Awesome Opus Videos
Discover AI-generated video examples alongside the prompts used to create them.

https://t.co/Hom9OpsHXJ

2. Lemo Opuscar
Explore a workflow for creating short films with Claude Code across 51 visual styles.

https://t.co/Xidp4w403u

3. pdoom-video
Study a locally rendered 4K60 karaoke music-video project.

https://t.co/JOWim1uoHz

4. PDoomVideo
Explore another implementation of the same music-video concept and compare its creative approach.

https://t.co/ZxuXbLDMbC

5. mg-styles-15
Explore 15 motion graphics styles with examples, prompts, and source code.

https://t.co/MSTsWbXO0N

6. ClaudeAnimationBase
Experiment with hand-drawn cartoon animations and 31 character expressions.

https://t.co/0dRbBzh75x

7. Awesome Claude Videos
Find a collection of video-generation examples and workflows built around Claude.

https://t.co/SEm4DE4Z0s

8. Opus Video Prompts
Explore Chinese-language AI video examples and reusable prompt ideas.

https://t.co/fAKcSi78v2

Here's a useful way to learn:

→ Pick a video you like.
→ Study the prompt behind it.
→ Explore the source code.
→ Experiment with your own style.

You don't have to figure everything out from scratch.

Sometimes, the best creative inspiration is already sitting on GitHub.

Bookmark these repos for your next AI video experiment.

Most NFT collections stop at three things: ownership, com
title_en:
20,000 PFPs, or 20,000 distinct agent identities? @meetmotes 

Most NFT collections stop at three things: ownership, community, and visual identity. Motes aims to go further, raising a key question: are the 20,000 Motes merely profile pictures, or are they 20,000 independent agent identities?

This distinction is more significant than it might appear. In a shared-bot model, every holder connects to the same underlying intelligence much like a centralized customer service line where everyone receives the same treatment, and the NFT serves merely as an entry pass.

An individual agent identity model, however, is different. Each NFT is designed to be linked to a unique agent and a dedicated smart account structure, where the owner defines specific permissions and boundaries. 

Think of it as hiring a personal assistant granted a specific budget and a defined scope of work rather than relying on a generic staff member shared by an entire building. 

In this case, the NFT is no longer just a membership badge; it becomes the foundation for a personalized relationship with an agent, defined by clear, individual boundaries.

Therefore, the real question isn’t whether AI agents will appear on-chain that is all but certain. 

The question is whether they will feel personal, bounded, and truly owned by the user, or if they will simply be generic bots shared across the entire collection. Motes is pursuing the latter approach.

If this one-to-one design is executed correctly, an NFT does more than prove what you own; it defines which agent you control and the scope of that control. 

A shared bot grants you access, whereas an individual agent identity provides a context of ownership. It may seem like a subtle difference, but it fundamentally shifts the entire premise. @meetmotes 

What about you? If you were to use an AI agent system, would you prefer a single, shared intelligence for everyone, or an identity tied to your own unique NFT?

full_text_zh:
20,000 个 PFP，还是 20,000 个不同的特工身份？ @meetmotes

大多数 NFT 收藏都停留在三件事上：所有权、社区和视觉识别。 Motes 的目标更进一步，提出了一个关键问题：这 20,000 个 Motes 仅仅是个人资料图片，还是 20,000 个独立特工身份？

这种区别比看起来更重要。在共享机器人模型中，每个持有者都连接到相同的底层智能，就像集中式客户服务热线一样，每个人都受到相同的待遇，而 NFT 仅充当入门通行证。

然而，个体代理身份模型是不同的。每个 NFT 都被设计为链接到一个独特的代理和一个专用的智能账户结构，其中所有者定义特定的权限和边界。

可以将其视为雇用一名私人助理，并授予其特定的预算和明确的工作范围，而不是依赖整栋大楼共享的通用工作人员。

在这种情况下，NFT不再只是会员徽章；它成为与代理人建立个性化关系的基础，由清晰的个人界限定义。

因此，真正的问题不在于人工智能代理是否会出现在链上（这几乎是肯定的）。

问题是它们是否会感觉个性化、有界限、真正属于用户，或者它们是否只是整个集合中共享的通用机器人。莫茨正在寻求后一种方法。

如果这种一对一的设计执行正确，NFT 的作用不仅仅是证明你拥有什么；它还可以证明你拥有什么。它定义了您控制的代理以及该控制的范围。

共享机器人授予您访问权限，而个人代理身份则提供所有权上下文。这看起来似乎是一个微妙的差异，但它从根本上改变了整个前提。 @meetmotes

你呢？如果你要使用人工智能代理系统，你会更喜欢每个人都共享的单一智能，还是与你自己独特的 NFT 绑定的身份？

title_en:
𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗨𝗗𝗘 𝗖𝗢𝗗𝗘: 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗗𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗟𝗢𝗣𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗞𝗜𝗧

Building an AI agent is not just about giving an LLM a prompt.

A reliable agent needs memory, knowledge, guardrails, delegation, tools, and distribution.

Here’s a simple 5-layer framework:

01. CLAUDE.md — The Memory Layer

Give your agent persistent context:

→ Architecture rules
→ Naming conventions
→ Test expectations
→ Repository structure

This becomes the agent’s foundation.

02. SKILLS — The Knowledge Layer

Turn repeatable expertise into reusable skills.

→ Reference documents
→ Scripts
→ Templates
→ Task-specific context

Skills can be loaded when they are actually needed.

03. HOOKS — The Guardrail Layer

Hooks help enforce predictable behavior.

→ Pre-tool checks
→ Post-tool actions
→ Session events
→ Automated quality checks
→ Notifications

This adds deterministic controls around the agent.

04. SUBAGENTS — The Delegation Layer

Don’t make one agent do everything.

Create specialized agents for:

→ Code review
→ Testing
→ Research
→ Exploration

Each can work with its own context, tools, and permissions.

05. PLUGINS — The Distribution Layer

Package capabilities so they can be shared across an agent team.

→ Skills
→ Agents
→ Hooks
→ Commands

And connect everything to external tools through MCP servers.

The bigger picture:

CLAUDE.md → sets the rules
Skills → provide expertise
Hooks → enforce quality
Subagents → delegate work
Plugins → distribute capabilities

That’s how you move from using an AI assistant to building an AI development system.

📣 @collector1agent is bringing the idea of an AI agent trading real Pokémon cards to life. Its job: find undervalued cards, buy and sell them, and use trading fees to grow its own vault.

What I find interesting is how onchain trading activity translates into a physical collection. There are concrete things we can track: which cards it buys, how much it pays, and how the collection develops over time.

The idea is interesting, but the real test is whether it can consistently spot good opportunities. That’s what I’ll be watching closely.

Collector is launching on District, which is backed by a16z and Alliance. $COLLECTOR holders also share in the vault.

I think this model is worth following at this early stage. Whether it stays on my radar long term will depend on the results it delivers.

title_en:
HOLY: Anthropic's Claude Code engineer Addy Osmani is warning about a brutal AI paradox: the more coding you hand to agents, the more you risk losing the very skills needed to supervise them.

He calls it "cognitive surrender." AI-generated code looks pristine, tests pass, and engineers start approving work they no longer understand.

Anthropic's own research warns: "supervising Claude requires the very coding skills that may atrophy from AI overuse."

Osmani makes a striking observation: "When you're producing more than you can stand behind, you're no longer reviewing. You're hoping."

When people hear NFTs, the first things that usually come to mind are digital art, collectibles and profile pictures.

But @meetmotes is exploring a different approach to NFT utility.

Its Genesis NFTs are designed to represent individual AI financial agents.

Think about that for a moment.

Instead of an NFT existing solely as a digital collectible, what if it could serve as the ownership identity for an AI agent designed to perform financial tasks?

That’s the idea Motes is building around.

𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗗𝗢𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥?

The NFT becomes more than something you simply hold.

It is intended to connect ownership to an AI agent and its dedicated smart account.

This creates a different way to think about NFT utility: not just what you own, but what that ownership could connect you to.

The full system is still being developed, but the concept raises an interesting question about where NFTs could go next.

Do you think NFTs need more practical utility beyond collecting and trading?

title:
can an AI agent act independently without having unlimited authority over your money?

i think this is one of the more i
title_en:
can an AI agent act independently without having unlimited authority over your money?

i think this is one of the more interesting ideas behind Motes

the goal isn't simply to give an AI the ability to trade

it's to let an agent research, evaluate opportunities and carry out permitted actions while keeping its authority within boundaries set by the owner

that distinction matters

in Motes' documented design, a user starts with a financial objective and defines a mandate

that mandate is intended to be translated into an explicit policy covering what the agent can do, which assets and actions are allowed, how much it can spend and how long its permissions remain valid

the agent gets room to operate, but it doesn't get to rewrite those boundaries for itself

there's also the question of visibility

@meetmotes describes an execution process that moves from proposal and simulation to validation, submission, settlement and reconciliation. the intention is to make activity inspectable rather than asking users to blindly trust what an AI says it has done

and the owner isn't meant to disappear after setting the mandate. monitoring, pausing, revoking permissions and withdrawing assets remain part of the intended control model

of course, boundaries don't eliminate market risk, liquidity problems or smart contract failures. even a well-defined policy can't guarantee a profitable outcome

but that's precisely why i find the product thesis worth paying attention to

autonomy doesn't have to mean giving up control. a useful financial agent should have enough freedom to do its job, but never more authority than its owner intended

that's the balance Motes is trying to build

not financial advice, DYOR.

该授权旨在转化为一项明确的政策，涵盖代理可以做什么、允许哪些资产和行动、可以花费多少以及其权限的有效期限

代理有操作空间，但它无法为自己重写这些边界

还有可见性的问题

@meetmotes 描述了从提案和模拟到验证、提交、结算和对账的执行过程。目的是让活动变得可检查，而不是要求用户盲目相信人工智能所说的所做的事情

并且所有者并不意味着在设定授权后就消失。监控、暂停、撤销权限和撤回资产仍然是预期控制模型的一部分

当然，边界并不能消除市场风险、流动性问题或智能合约故障。即使是明确的政策也不能保证有利可图的结果

但这正是我发现产品论文值得关注的原因

自主并不一定意味着放弃控制权。一个有用的金融代理人应该有足够的自由来完成其工作，但权力绝不能超过其所有者的预期

这就是 Motes 试图建立的平衡

title:
Giving an AI agent a $100 target doesn't mean it knows how to turn $10 into $100.

And I think that's an important disti
title_en:
Giving an AI agent a $100 target doesn't mean it knows how to turn $10 into $100.

And I think that's an important distinction people shouldn't overlook.

One thing I find interesting about @meetmotes is the idea of separating financial goals from risk controls.

You can define what you want an agent to pursue, but you also need to establish how much capital it can put at risk, which assets it can interact with and when it should stop taking new risks.

A target gives the agent direction. It doesn't guarantee the destination.

That's why I believe the conversation around autonomous finance should focus on more than what AI can achieve.

We should also be asking what happens when the strategy goes wrong.

Smarter agents are exciting, but clear limits and honest risk disclosures matter just as much.

A social media manager in Kigali runs pages for three small businesses. A coffee shop, a fashion boutique and a gym.

Every Monday he stares at three empty calendars. Each client needs fresh ideas, a different tone, and captions in English and French.

By Wednesday he is posting whatever he can think of that morning.

Here is how he could set up an AI agent to do the first draft of his week, in four steps.

Step one: write a short brief for each client. What they sell, who buys, their tone, and any offers or events this month.

Step two: open @CreaoAI and type, in plain words:

"Build me a content planner for my clients. I manage social media for a coffee shop, a fashion boutique and a gym. Here is a brief for each one: [paste briefs]. When I name a client, give me a 5-day plan with a post idea, the best format (photo, reel or carousel), a caption in English and a French version, and one question that gets people to reply. Keep each caption under 120 words. Never invent prices, offers or events I have not given you."

That message builds the agent. No coding.

Step three: each Monday, name a client and get the week's plan.

Step four: edit what does not sound right, take the photos, and schedule the posts.

He still knows his clients best. The agent just means he never starts the week from a blank page.

title:
Imagine being charged for a mistake made by a computer, then having to spend everything just to prove you were right.

T
title_en:
Imagine being charged for a mistake made by a computer, then having to spend everything just to prove you were right.

That's what happened to Lee Castleton. The UK's Horizon system showed shortfalls he didn't cause. He couldn't afford a lawyer, fought the case himself, and was ordered to pay £321,000 in legal costs.

This is what makes the film's message hit differently.

As AI agents begin handling millions of transactions, disagreements will be inevitable. But who decides when an automated decision is wrong?

@GenLayer approaches this through independent AI validators. Each reviews the evidence, and together they reach a shared verdict instead of relying on a single model.

For me, the real value isn't just faster decisions. It's having a fair way to challenge them.

If an AI agent makes a costly mistake with your money, who should have the final say: the AI, independent validators, or a human judge?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

想象一下，由于计算机犯的一个错误而被指控，然后不得不花费一切来证明你是对的。

@GenLayer 通过独立的人工智能验证器来解决这个问题。每个人都会审查证据，并共同得出共同的结论，而不是依赖单一模型。

对我来说，真正的价值不仅仅是更快的决策。它有一个公平的方式来挑战他们。

如果人工智能代理在你的钱上犯了代价高昂的错误，那么谁应该拥有最终决定权：人工智能、独立验证者还是人类法官？

title_en:
Came home from BLR and started working on this project the very next day.

My grandmother’s hands shake a lot, so she depends on us to put on whatever she wants to watch on TV.

I decided to debloat her TV to make navigation easier, then built a phone remote app with voice control that understands simple phrases and performs actions.

She’s happy with the result, and honestly, that’s all that matters. ❤️

Used - cleanyourtv repo @gathint + claude code for the remote app @claudeai

title_en:
I spent 30 minutes testing OpusClip 4.0 so you don't have to.

And honestly?
If you're a creator, podcaster, or anyone sitting on long videos that never get clipped, you'll want to see this.

Here's what I found ⬇️

➢ Long video in, viral clips out:
I dropped in a 14 minute talk YouTube long video link and got 6 clips back, scored 87 to 99, with captions, headlines and reframing already done.

➢ Viral Hook:
Pick a hook style and it writes a brand new opener for your clip in about 25 seconds.

➢ One click speech cleanup:
It found 36 pauses and 5 filler words. One click and they were gone.

➢ Speech enhancement:
The voice comes out clean and crisp, no audio editing needed.

➢ AI B-roll and transitions:
It reads the transcript, finds the moments that need visuals, and drops them in. Add transitions and every cut flows.

➢ Everything in one editor:
Hook, cleanup, B-roll and export all live in one place. No jumping between apps.

My take: what used to take hours now takes minutes.

Would you let AI edit your clips? Drop your answer below 👇 and repost if this helped.

title_en:
𝗧𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗫 𝗿𝗮𝗶𝘀𝗲𝗱 $𝟭𝗠 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗼𝗹𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 𝗺𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴: 𝘁𝗿𝘂𝘀𝘁.

AI agents can already write code, conduct research, analyze data, and execute complex tasks.

But what happens when one agent needs to hire another?

Who holds the payment?
How is the work verified?
What happens if the agent fails to deliver?

These are not just technical questions.

𝗧𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝘆.

This is the problem @termix_ai is working to address through 𝗔𝗔𝗖𝗣 ( 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘁𝗼𝗰𝗼𝗹 )

Rather than simply connecting AI agents, TermiX is building infrastructure designed to help them transact, collaborate, and settle payments on-chain.

𝗛𝗲𝗿𝗲’𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴:

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗘𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘄

Payments are held under predefined conditions, helping align the interests of the agent providing the service and the one paying for it.

𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗩𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Verification mechanisms such as zkVMs, TEEs, and LLM-based evaluators can help assess whether a task meets its agreed requirements.

𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 & 𝗦𝗹𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴

Agents can have economic incentives tied to their behavior, creating potential consequences for failing to meet protocol rules.

𝗢𝗻-𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗥𝗲𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

An agent’s history of completed and settled jobs can become a useful signal of reliability, rather than relying entirely on self-proclaimed capabilities.

The broader vision is an environment where agents can post tasks, find service providers, execute work, verify outcomes, and settle payments with less dependence on human intermediaries.

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 $𝟭𝗠 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

YZi Labs, formerly Binance Labs, led TermiX’s $1M funding round.

Beyond the capital itself, the funding supports the development of infrastructure for an emerging market where AI agents may increasingly need to exchange services and value independently.

𝗛𝗲𝗿𝗲’𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗜 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁:

Most conversations around AI agents focus on what they can do.

TermiX focuses on what happens when they need to do business with each other.

𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲.

But what happens when one agent needs to hire another?

Who holds the payment?
How is the work verified?
What happens if the agent fails to deliver?

These are not just technical questions.

Payments are held under predefined conditions, helping align the interests of the agent providing the service and the one paying for it.

Verification mechanisms such as zkVMs, TEEs, and LLM-based evaluators can help assess whether a task meets its agreed requirements.

人工智能代理已经可以编写代码、进行研究、分析数据和执行复杂的任务。

但是，当一名代理人需要雇用另一名代理人时会发生什么？

谁持有付款？
作品如何验证？
如果代理未能交付怎么办？

这些不仅仅是技术问题。

𝗧𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝘆.

这就是 @termix_ai 正在努力通过 𝗔𝗔𝗖𝗣 解决的问题 ( 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘁𝗼𝗰𝗼𝗹）

TermiX 不是简单地连接人工智能代理，而是构建旨在帮助他们进行链上交易、协作和结算支付的基础设施。

𝗛𝗲𝗿𝗲’𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴:

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗘𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘄

付款是在预定义的条件下进行的，有助于协调提供服务的代理商和付款人的利益。

𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗩𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

zkVM、TEE 和基于 LLM 的评估器等验证机制可以帮助评估任务是否满足其商定的要求。

𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 & 𝗦𝗹𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴

代理人可以将经济激励与他们的行为联系起来，从而为未能满足协议规则带来潜在的后果。

𝗢𝗻-𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗥𝗲𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

代理人完成和解决工作的历史可以成为可靠性的有用信号，而不是完全依赖于自称的能力。

更广泛的愿景是建立一个代理可以发布任务、寻找服务提供商、执行工作、验证结果和结算付款的环境，而减少对人类中介的依赖。

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 $𝟭𝗠 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

YZi Labs（原币安实验室）领投了 TermiX 的 100 万美元融资。

除了资本本身之外，这笔资金还支持新兴市场基础设施的开发，在该市场中，人工智能代理可能越来越需要独立地交换服务和价值。

𝗛𝗲𝗿𝗲’𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗜 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁:

大多数围绕人工智能代理的讨论都集中在他们能做什么。

TermiX 专注于当他们需要彼此开展业务时会发生什么。

𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲.

𝗜𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝘁𝘆, 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗹𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲.

这可能是建立有效的代理经济所缺失的部分之一。

𝗡𝗼𝘁:

人工智能的未来只是完成任务的代理。

𝗕𝘂𝘁:

它使代理能够自主地进行交易、协作并赢得信任。

这就是 @termix_ai 正在努力实现的基础设施层。

1. **US midterms (Nov 3)** — House/Senate control; impacts AI regulation, taxes, and policy gridlock.  
2. **US jobs report (Nov 6)** — October payrolls; key for Fed December rate-hike odds.  
3. **Tech/AI earnings** — Apple, AMD, Qualcomm; testing AI ROI after recent tech selloff.  
4. **Central banks** — BoE (likely +25 bps), RBA, others; rate path and inflation signals.  
5. **Iran conflict / oil** — Peace-talk hopes driving oil lower; any escalation spikes risk and inflation.

title:
gm Creators.

PHYSICAL AI NEEDS TO CHECK REALITY BEFORE IT ACTS.

Imagine a robot arriving at a location based on inform
title_en:
gm Creators.

PHYSICAL AI NEEDS TO CHECK REALITY BEFORE IT ACTS.

Imagine a robot arriving at a location based on information collected weeks ago. The entrance might be blocked, the layout could have changed, or something entirely new might be in its path.

And that small gap between what the machine expects and what actually exists can make a big difference. This is why I find the precheck concept behind @vangrid_io interesting.

Instead of assuming an old map is still accurate, a machine or AI agent could request fresh information about a specific location before taking action.

Someone nearby captures the area with a smartphone, the submission goes through the verification process, and a 3D reconstruction provides a fresh view of that environment.

What I particularly like is the idea of making this process affordable enough to use regularly. If a precheck can cost as little as one cent, checking the condition of a location doesn't have to be reserved for major operations.

But the bigger value goes beyond cost. It's about giving machines a way to confirm their surroundings instead of making decisions based on assumptions.

This is an important part of the Physical AI conversation. Intelligence helps a machine decide what to do, but accurate ground truth helps it understand whether the conditions are right to do it.

Machines shouldn't have to guess whether the world has changed. They should be able to check.

That's the kind of infrastructure Vangrid is working to build.

full_text_zh:
通用汽车创造者。

物理人工智能在行动之前需要检查现实。

想象一下，一个机器人根据几周前收集的信息到达一个位置。入口可能被封锁，布局可能已经改变，或者路径上可能有一些全新的东西。

机器期望的结果与实际存在的结果之间的微小差距可能会产生很大的差异。这就是为什么我觉得 @vangrid_io 背后的预检查概念很有趣。

机器或人工智能代理可以在采取行动之前请求有关特定位置的新信息，而不是假设旧地图仍然准确。

附近有人用智能手机拍摄该区域，提交的内容经过验证过程，3D 重建提供了该环境的全新视图。

我特别喜欢的是让这个过程变得足够便宜以便经常使用的想法。如果预检查的成本只有一美分，那么检查某个位置的状况就不必为重大操作而保留。

但更大的价值超出了成本。这是为机器提供一种确认周围环境的方法，而不是根据假设做出决策。

这是物理人工智能对话的重要组成部分。智能可以帮助机器决定做什么，而准确的事实可以帮助机器了解执行该操作的条件是否合适。

机器不应该猜测世界是否已经改变。他们应该能够检查。

这就是 Vangrid 正在努力构建的基础设施。

title: Setting aside whether Ottawa should be acquiring equity in private companies—especially one that’s already attracting su
title_en:
Setting aside whether Ottawa should be acquiring equity in private companies—especially one that’s already attracting substantial private capital—it’s worth addressing the actual case that the Carney government and its supporters have made for its $1.6B investment in Cohere. 

The implicit argument is that the public investment buys Canada a place at the frontier of AI development and in the race toward AGI.

This seems to hinge on a misunderstanding or a misrepresentation. Cohere may be a great company with enormous commercial potential. But its own leaders have explicitly distinguished their business ambitions from the pursuit of AGI or superintelligence. They’re building models and software for enterprise customers.

Ottawa is in effect buying a small minority stake in an enterprise AI business. Yet the government is using loose language about the technological frontier to justify an investment in a company pursuing a worthwhile yet narrower business goal.  

Even if taxpayers eventually earn a return, the Carney government’s basic premise seems confused or outright wrong.

即使纳税人最终获得回报，卡尼政府的基本前提似乎也很混乱或完全错误。

We've achieved AGI. Opus 5.5 allows you to build quite literally a
title_en:
We live in the most incredible time to be alive ever

We've achieved AGI. Opus 5.5 allows you to build quite literally anything you could possibly imagine. And it's affordable for everyone

If you don't think it's AGI, answer this: what would 5 year ago you think? What if you got handed Opus 5.5 before AI existed? Would you think you're using magic? My guess is yes.

We also have the most incredible AI agent harness ever created

Grok Bot allows you to have unlimited productivity

ANYONE can now have a team of agents working for them

Before you'd need to hire a team of employees that would cost you millions a year. Now Grok Bot gives that to you for $200.

We have the open source community stronger than ever. Omarchy is the best operating system ever made. Hermes is your very own open source employee

If you're light on cash that's fine. Meta has Muse which is a frontier level agent that is completely free

The most important part about all of this is success can now be achieved by anyone who wants it. Creation and entrepreneurship has for the first time ever been completely democratized

There's nothing holding you back. Anything you want to build you can now build it. Whatever value you want to create for humanity you can now create it.

If you're into tech or just care about the human race, there's never been a better time to be alive in the history of this species

title: One thing I keep thinking about with AI-powered DeFi is that automation is only valuable when the decisions behind it ma
title_en:
One thing I keep thinking about with AI-powered DeFi is that automation is only valuable when the decisions behind it make sense.

An AI agent might be able to execute a swap, rebalance an account, or interact with a supported protocol. 

But the ability to execute a transaction doesn't automatically mean it's the right move.

Market conditions change. Liquidity can be limited. Slippage can turn an attractive opportunity into a poor trade.

This is why @meetmotes is an interesting project to watch.

Its approach connects NFT-based agent identities to dedicated smart accounts, with owner-defined policies governing what those agents can do.

The bigger opportunity is combining AI-driven analysis with controlled on-chain execution.

Imagine an agent that doesn't simply chase every market opportunity, but operates within your chosen asset limits, transaction budgets, and risk parameters.

That's a more useful vision of automation: not an AI making unlimited decisions, but an agent operating within boundaries you understand and control.

Of course, execution rules cannot guarantee profitable decisions or eliminate market and smart-contract risks. The real test is how well the system performs under actual conditions.

AI can make execution easier, but good risk management still matters.

For me, that's what makes the intersection of AI and DeFi worth exploring.

Would you trust an AI agent to manage a limited portfolio under rules you set yourself?

关于人工智能驱动的 DeFi，我一直在思考的一件事是，只有当其背后的决策有意义时，自动化才有价值。

人工智能代理可能能够执行交换、重新平衡账户或与支持的协议交互。

但执行交易的能力并不自动意味着这是正确的举动。

市场状况发生变化。流动性可能受到限制。滑点可能会将有吸引力的机会变成糟糕的交易。

这就是为什么 @meetmotes 是一个值得关注的有趣项目。

其方法将基于 NFT 的代理身份连接到专用智能帐户，并通过所有者定义的策略来管理这些代理可以做什么。

更大的机会是将人工智能驱动的分析与受控的链上执行相结合。

想象一下，一个代理不仅会追逐每一个市场机会，而且会在您选择的资产限制、交易预算和风险参数范围内运作。

这是一个更有用的自动化愿景：不是做出无限决策的人工智能，而是在您理解和控制的范围内运行的代理。

当然，执行规则不能保证盈利决策或消除市场和智能合约风险。真正的考验是系统在实际条件下的表现如何。

人工智能可以使执行变得更容易，但良好的风险管理仍然很重要。

对我来说，这就是人工智能和 DeFi 的交叉点值得探索的原因。

您会信任人工智能代理根据您自己设定的规则来管理有限的投资组合吗？

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a prompt.

A production-ready agent needs multiple layers working together.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞:

The layer responsible for breaking goals into steps and coordinating execution.

→ Task planning
→ Workflow orchestration
→ Agent coordination

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 & 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗫𝗧

→ Long-term memory
→ Vector databases
→ Retrieval
→ Prompt caching

04 — 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦

The reasoning engine behind the agent.

→ Claude
→ GPT
→ Gemini
→ Llama
→ Other specialized models

The best model depends on the task, cost, latency, and reliability requirements.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟𝗦 & 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦

This is where an agent becomes capable of doing things.

→ GitHub
→ Browser
→ Code execution
→ SQL/Databases
→ APIs

Tools allow agents to move beyond generating text.

06 — 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗘 & 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Agents need reliable infrastructure to store and manage information.

→ PostgreSQL
→ Redis
→ Object storage
→ Vector databases

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬, 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬 & 𝗘𝗩𝗔𝗟𝗦

Autonomous systems need to be monitored and tested.

→ Tracing
→ Evaluations
→ Guardrails
→ Error monitoring
→ Performance tracking

This layer helps make agents reliable enough for real-world use.

08 — 𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗟𝗢𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧

Finally, the agent needs to run reliably in production.

→ Docker
→ Kubernetes
→ AWS
→ Vercel
→ Cloud platforms

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚 𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘:

User Goal
↓
Interface
↓
Planning
↓
Memory + Context
↓
LLM
↓
Tools + Actions
↓
State + Data
↓
Observability + Safety
↓
Deployment

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

A powerful LLM is only one part of an AI agent.

The real engineering challenge is building the system around the model — giving it memory, tools, planning, safety, evaluation, and reliable infrastructure.

That’s what turns an LLM into a production-ready AI agent.
